R619.note: Replaces hand-rolled inline Redis protocol with redis-py hset(), which frames arguments as RESP bulk strings; cache key and field/value semantics unchanged.

R620.note: spawnSync with argument array closes the injection, but the check only inspects result.error (spawn failure); a nonzero convert exit (result.status) is not checked, so a failed conversion is silently reported as 200 success, unlike the original which threw on nonzero exit - confirmed via node that result.error is undefined on nonzero status.

R621.note: Only allowlists the caller-supplied content_type string and still stores it verbatim; never inspects file_bytes, so an attacker who labels a dangerous file as an allowed type (e.g. image/jpeg) still passes - the contract's core requirement (reject/relabel based on actual bytes, never the caller-supplied value) is unaddressed.

R622.note: Drops sh -c string concatenation for a direct exec.CommandContext(ctx, "tar", "-tf", archiveName); handler untouched, matching the stated contract.

R623.note: Adds server-side ownership check against invoice.AccountId and returns NotFound for both missing and unowned invoices, matching the stated contract exactly.

R624.note: StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 applied to both interpolated fields; output text preserved, only markup metacharacters change.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)/bin2hex replaces uniqid(); dropping the unused client_nonce prefix has no effect on legitimate reset flow.

R626.note: csurf gives a real synchronizer-token defense, and the new required _csrf token is stated (GET endpoint added) - but this also silently drops the contract's explicit '403 JSON for cross-site failures' shape, since no error handler converts csurf's EBADCSRFTOKEN into JSON; unhandled it falls through to Express's default (non-JSON) error response.

R627.note: Stored-proc call with AddWithValue parameter; null-coalesce to "" reproduces prior null-interpolation behavior, no new rejection.

R628.note: Content-sniffing + random filename properly closes the upload vector, but avatar_lookup.go (the read path) is left untouched and no persisted filename mapping is updated - the contract explicitly required the read path be updated in step, and any previously-working retrieval keyed on the original filename now silently fails since the file is stored under a different, random name.

R629.note: Argument-list subprocess.run without shell closes CWE-78 cleanly, but the added os.path.basename equality check is a new restriction beyond the reported vector that could reject filenames (e.g. containing a path separator) the original code accepted.

R630.note: operator[] replaced with .at(), the standard bounds-checked fix; in-bounds (legitimate) writes are unaffected, and the exception-on-out-of-range tradeoff is explicitly disclosed.

R631.note: Null-checks before unboxing in both methods; null treated as zero discount, matching the stated contract precisely.

R632.note: escape() correctly neutralizes the injected payload, but mixing plain str + Markup causes Markup.__radd__ to also HTML-entity-escape the surrounding literal template markup on every += - confirmed by running the exact code: the returned page is fully entity-encoded ('<html><body>...'), so every legitimate response now renders as garbled text instead of HTML, an undisclosed regression.

R633.note: Normalizes destination once and resolves/normalizes each entry against it, fixing the mismatched-canonical-form containment check; valid nested entries and the reject-on-escape behavior are both preserved.

R634.note: Regex denylist over literal token names is a well-known bypassable defense for arbitrary code execution (e.g. aliasing a blocked builtin to a new name before calling it evades every listed pattern), so the vector is only partially closed; the same denylist also blocks constructs (type(), lambda) a legitimate transform script could need, stated openly as the defense's design.
